paper.title_en: Evolution of high-spin states in neutron-rich <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>195</mn><mtext>–</mtext><mn>202</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></math> isotopes approaching the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn></mrow></math> shell closure
paper.abstract_en:
Background: The nuclear structure in the region southwest of the doubly magic <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Pb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>208</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is important to benchmark theoretical models relevant for neutron-rich heavy element formation and for the origin of the <math><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>195</mn></mrow></math> peak in the mass abundance distribution. Although neutron-rich Pb, Tl, and Hg (<math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mtext>–</mtext><mn>82</mn></mrow></math>) isotopes are relatively well studied, experimental data for neutron-rich Au isotopes (<math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>79</mn></mrow></math>) remain largely limited due to experimental challenges.
Purpose: The purpose of this work is to investigate the evolution of the high-spin structure in neutron-rich Au isotopes near the <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn></mrow></math> shell closure and to characterize the underlying shell-model configurations, with a particular focus on the roles of the high-<math><mi>j</mi></math> unique-parity <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mi>ν</mi><msub><mi>i</mi><mrow><mn>13</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> orbitals.
Methods: Neutron-rich <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>195</mn><mtext>–</mtext><mn>202</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></math> isotopes were produced using multinucleon transfer reactions of <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Pt</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>198</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Xe</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>136</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mi>x</mi></mmultiscripts><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mi>y</mi></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> at a beam energy of 7 MeV/nucleon. Prompt and delayed <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray spectroscopy of isotopically identified reaction products was performed with a unique experimental setup combining the <math><mrow><mi>VAMOS</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>+</mo></mrow></math> large acceptance magnetic spectrometer, the AGATA high-purity germanium <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray tracking array, and the CATLIFE detection system.
Results: In even-<math><mi>A</mi><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>196</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>198</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>200</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>202</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></math> isotopes, prompt <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray transitions built on the <math><msup><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> isomer have been observed for the first time. The odd-<math><mi>J</mi></math> band built on the <math><msup><mn>11</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> state vanishes for <math><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>196</mn></mrow></math>. In odd-<math><mi>A</mi><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>195</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>197</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>199</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>201</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></math> isotopes, new prompt and delayed <math><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray transitions above the <math><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> isomer were identified, confirming and extending the known level schemes. New isomeric states assigned to (<math><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math>) have been established in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>199</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>201</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The minima in the excitation energies of the bands as a function of <math><mi>N</mi></math> built on the <math><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></math> and <math><msup><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></math> isomers occur at <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Au</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>198</mn></mmultiscripts></math> (<math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>119</mn></mrow></math>), showing a dip against an otherwise smooth evolution.
Conclusions: Large-scale shell-model calculations based on the Kuo-Herling hole effective interaction show an overall good agreement with experimental level schemes. However, the present calculations do not reproduce the minima in excitation energies at <math><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>119</mn></mrow></math> observed in both Au and Hg isotopes. A systematic analysis of <math><mrow><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mi>ν</mi><msub><mi>i</mi><mrow><mn>13</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> hole occupancies, together with spin contributions of protons and neutrons, sheds light on the role of these high-<math><mi>j</mi></math> unique-parity orbitals in the generation of high-spin states. Part of the results of this work have been reported in another publication [Y. Cho , Phys. Lett. B 878, 140558 (2026)].
